first_impression.reaction: My assistant shortlisted it, so I gave it the first screen. The opening line is confident and not salesy, which I like. But it's a primer on the 4Cs and checking a report number. Our jeweller does that. My assistant can read the rest and tell me if there's anything on the planning side. There's very little.

journey.quote: Most advice on choosing a diamond is written by someone with a tray of stones to sell you.
journey.reaction: Good opening. Calm, no pitch. It made me think the brand has some taste.

journey.quote: As at October 2026, jewellery bought overseas counts toward the AUD900 general goods duty-free allowance, so declare a ring that takes you over it.
journey.reaction: Correct, I'm sure, but a duty-free allowance in the key takeaways tells me straight away who this page is written for. It isn't me.

journey.section: Checking the report number on the lab's own site
journey.reaction: A bit eager. My assistant or the jeweller handles this anyway.

journey.quote: Travel with copies of the grading report and receipt, kept separately from the ring itself.
journey.reaction: Sensible. The travel part is the only bit close to my world, but it stops at hand luggage. No mention of private transfers or security for a valuable piece.

journey.section: From the ring to the destination
journey.quote: Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, with one Wedded Advisor as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: One point of contact is what I want. Nothing about scale or discretion though.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Wonderland delivered weddings of 200 to 400 guests?
Can they arrange exclusive use of a property and coordinate with our own security team?
How do they protect privacy (vendor confidentiality, no social posting)?
Is there a private or referral route rather than a public enquiry link?
Can they arrange secure transport or courier for high-value jewellery at an overseas wedding?

turn_offs_found.quote: Buying the stone abroad, or carrying it to a proposal overseas, is workable with a little paperwork.
turn_offs_found.why: Reads as written for a standard traveller. For a significant piece it isn't 'a little paperwork', it's security and insurance.

cta_reaction.quote: If the proposal or the wedding is heading overseas, talk to a Wedded Concierge about a proposal or wedding abroad.
cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a public link from a buying guide. Nothing here shows they handle my numbers or keep things private. A referral or a private-client contact would change that.

top_3_changes: Move the AUD900 duty-free line out of the key takeaways and keep it in the travel section; it sets a mass-market tone on the first screen.
In the travel section, add one understated line on secure handling of valuable jewellery abroad (private transfers, insurer-approved transport), only if the brand can back it up.
Offer a quieter private-client or referral route next to the general concierge link.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
Ignored [[VERIFY]] markers, HTML comments and image slot notes
Did not invent problems; low relevance is down to topic fit, not quality

assumptions: Persona is provisional and uncalibrated; this is a top-of-funnel diamond guide not aimed at UHNW, so low relevance is expected and should carry limited weight.
